newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen drifting in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen drifting in narrow range.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to drift in a narrow range on Friday, as yesterday's rebound after losses over a racketeer scandal is unlikely to continue due to a lack of buying factors, brokers said.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average climbed 118.61 points or 0.59 percent to finish at 20,331.43. Its September futures jumped 110 to 20,330.

"The Nikkei 225 did not fall through 20,000 yesterday, and this gave us the impression that the downside was solid," said a market analyst at a foreign securities house. "But there are no fresh buying factors to sustain the rebound."
Brokers said that the Nikkei 225 index would be trapped in a range of 20,000 to 20,500 for a while.
"I don't think the Nikkei 225 will move drastically until late August," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.

On Thursday, the key index slipped initially on worries over a widening racketeer scandal and over the financial woes of some companies in the construction sector, but the losses were erased later by gains in blue-chip issues, brokers said.
